versions.notes: 2024 rule (published 26 Apr 2024) effective 1 Jul 2024 except as applied to the State of Texas as an employer. VACATED nationwide by E.D. Tex. (Texas v. U.S. DOL, 15 Nov 2024) and N.D. Tex. (Flint Avenue, LLC v. U.S. DOL, 30 Dec 2024); Fifth Circuit dismissed the appeals 5 and 7 May 2026. Retained only as history; legal review needed on whether to treat it as void ab initio. The scheduled 1 Jan 2025 step ($1,128/wk, HCE $151,164) never took effect.

rules.description: FMLA employer coverage, employee eligibility, entitlement and 12-month period methods

versions.notes: Leave-year methods and military caregiver single 12-month period per DOL Fact Sheet #28H (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28h-fmla-12-month-period). Changing method requires 60 days notice.

value.federalContractorCriteria: federal contractors with 50 or more employees meeting certain criteria (EEOC)

versions.notes: Long-standing rule; in force before this date. Earlier history is not modelled — effectiveFrom is the modelling baseline, not the date the rule was enacted. STATUS (Oct 2026): 2024 collection closed; EEOC says updates on the 2025 collection will be posted. On 21 Jul 2026 the EEOC voted to issue an NPRM to rescind EEO-1 to EEO-6 reporting (see https://www.eeoc.gov/newsroom/eeoc-proposes-rescission-annual-race-and-sex-reporting-requirements). The requirement remains in the regulations until a final rule; review when the rule is finalised. Federal contractor criteria (e.g. contract value) not modelled.
